introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, answer all questions): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Figure 4* shows the fringe pattern obtained on a screen from Young's double-slit experiment to measure the wavelength of a **monochromatic light** (underlined in the paper) from a source.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_4_fig_1.png)

figures.legende: Figure 4 : five dark fringes (rectangles) on a screen, separated by bright fringes; a double arrow labelled 10.0 mm runs from the first dark fringe to the fifth dark fringe.

incertitudes: Question 4 : le sens de la cote « 10.0 mm » se lit sur la figure : la flèche va du centre de la première frange sombre au centre de la cinquième, soit quatre interfranges, donc 2,5 mm chacune. Lecture retenue : elle donne une longueur d'onde de 500 nm, valeur plausible. Seul le total (5 marks) est imprimé. Le groupe souligné de l énoncé (monochromatic light) est rendu en gras.

questions.enonce_markdown: Explain the meaning of the underlined phrase.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Monochromatic light** is light of a **single wavelength** (a single frequency, hence a single colour). Using it in Young's experiment gives sharp, well-defined bright and dark fringes of one colour, whereas white light would give coloured, overlapping fringes.

The 10.0 mm shown in figure 4 runs from the first to the fifth dark fringe, that is across **4 fringe separations** (there are 5 dark fringes, hence 4 gaps):

$$x = \frac{10.0\ \mathrm{mm}}{4} = 2.5\ \mathrm{mm}$$

**Fringe separation $x = 2.5\ \mathrm{mm} = 2.5\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If the distance from the double slits to the screen is $2.5\ \mathrm{m}$ while the separation of the double slits is $0.50\ \mathrm{mm}$, determine the wavelength of the light from the source.
questions.corrige_markdown:
For double-slit interference, $x = \dfrac{\lambda D}{a}$, so $\lambda = \dfrac{ax}{D}$ with $a = 0.50\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m}$, $D = 2.5\ \mathrm{m}$, $x = 2.5\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m}$:

$$\lambda = \frac{0.50\times10^{-3}\times2.5\times10^{-3}}{2.5} = 5.0\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{m}$$

**$\lambda = 5.0\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{m} = 500\ \mathrm{nm}$** (green light).
